> Original MUI X documentation: [Tree Item customization](https://mui.com/x/react-tree-view/tree-item-customization/). The examples of this page are written for R.

```{r setup, message = FALSE}
library(muiTreeView)
library(htmltools)
```

## Anatomy

Each Tree Item is made of parts, called slots: the `content` that wraps the row, the `iconContainer` with the expand and collapse icons, the `checkbox`, the `label` (and the `labelInput` when editing), and the `groupTransition` that wraps the children. [MUI docs](https://mui.com/x/react-tree-view/tree-item-customization/#anatomy)

```html
<li class="MuiTreeItem-root">
  <div class="MuiTreeItem-content">
    <div class="MuiTreeItem-iconContainer"></div>
    <button class="MuiTreeItem-checkbox"></button>
    <div class="MuiTreeItem-label"></div>
  </div>
  <ul class="MuiTreeItem-groupTransition"></ul>
</li>
```

Use `slotProps` to pass arguments, such as `sx` styles, to a slot, and `slots` to replace it with your own component.

### Content

Style the content of one item with `slotProps = list(content = ...)`. [MUI docs](https://mui.com/x/react-tree-view/tree-item-customization/#content)

```{r}
SimpleTreeView(
  TreeItem(
    itemId = "muiMaterial",
    label = "muiMaterial",
    slotProps = list(content = list(sx = list(bgcolor = "action.hover", borderRadius = 2)))
  ),
  TreeItem(itemId = "muiCharts", label = "muiCharts"),
  TreeItem(itemId = "reactRouter", label = "reactRouter")
)
```

### Label

Pass arguments to the label of an item with `slotProps = list(label = ...)`, for example an `id` to reference it, or styles. [MUI docs](https://mui.com/x/react-tree-view/tree-item-customization/#label)

```{r}
SimpleTreeView(
  TreeItem(
    itemId = "muiMaterial",
    label = "muiMaterial",
    slotProps = list(label = list(id = "muiMaterial-label", sx = list(fontStyle = "italic")))
  ),
  TreeItem(itemId = "muiCharts", label = "muiCharts")
)
```

### Checkbox

The checkbox is shown when `checkboxSelection = TRUE`. Style it with `slotProps = list(checkbox = ...)`. [MUI docs](https://mui.com/x/react-tree-view/tree-item-customization/#checkbox)

```{r}
SimpleTreeView(
  checkboxSelection = TRUE,
  multiSelect = TRUE,
  TreeItem(
    itemId = "muiMaterial",
    label = "muiMaterial",
    slotProps = list(checkbox = list(size = "small", color = "secondary"))
  ),
  TreeItem(
    itemId = "muiCharts",
    label = "muiCharts",
    slotProps = list(checkbox = list(size = "small", color = "secondary"))
  )
)
```

### Icon

Replace the icon of one item with `slots = list(icon = ...)`, a React component written with `JS()`:

```{r}
SimpleTreeView(
  TreeItem(itemId = "muiMaterial", label = "muiMaterial", slots = list(icon = JS("() => '★'"))),
  TreeItem(itemId = "muiCharts", label = "muiCharts", slots = list(icon = JS("() => '◆'"))),
  TreeItem(itemId = "reactRouter", label = "reactRouter")
)
```

To style all the items of a tree at once, use the `sx` argument of the tree with the CSS classes of the slots (`.MuiTreeItem-content`, `.MuiTreeItem-label`…), as shown in [Simple Tree View - Customization](simple-tree-view-customization.html#custom-styling). With `RichTreeView()`, use `slotProps = list(item = ...)`, as shown in [Rich Tree View - Customization](rich-tree-view-customization.html#style-some-items-with-slotprops).

## Basics

### Change nested item's indentation

Use `itemChildrenIndentation` to change the indentation of the children, 12px by default. [MUI docs](https://mui.com/x/react-tree-view/tree-item-customization/#change-nested-items-indentation)

```{r}
fns <- data.frame(
  package = c("muiMaterial", "muiMaterial", "muiCharts", "muiCharts", "reactRouter", "reactRouter"),
  fn = c("Button", "Drawer", "BarChart", "PieChart", "Route", "NavLink")
)

RichTreeView(
  items = asMuiTree(fns),
  itemChildrenIndentation = 32
)
```

The indentation is also available as the `--TreeView-itemChildrenIndentation` CSS variable, for example to align custom content with the items.

## Hooks

The hooks `useTreeItem()`, `useTreeItemUtils()` and `useTreeItemModel()` let you build your own Tree Item in React. From R, they can be used inside a component written with `JS()`, where `jsmodule['@mui/x-tree-view']` gives access to them. [Rich Tree View - Customization](rich-tree-view-customization.html#custom-tree-item) shows an item that uses `useTreeItemModel()` to read the data of the item. [MUI docs](https://mui.com/x/react-tree-view/tree-item-customization/#hooks)
